title: Integrated Security & Compliance Guidance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Risk Exceptions
author: Anita Kumar
body:
Purpose

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls and operational procedures across RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC, incident response for security incidents, compliance evidence collection workflows, and the process for managing risk exceptions. It is intended for security engineers, platform owners, compliance reviewers, and engineering leads responsible for implementing and operating controlled services.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood-managed services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Private deployments) and supporting infrastructure (IAM, logging, monitoring, build systems).
- Excludes personal development sandboxes that are explicitly scoped in team-level exceptions.

Summary of Responsibilities

- Security team: Maintain control definitions, run periodic evidence collection, own risk-exception approval gates.
- Eng-platform: Implement RBAC profiles, integrate audit logging for services, maintain KMS/HSM configuration for customer keys.
- Eng-sre: Ensure retention and retention enforcement in logging pipeline; own incident response runbooks and postmortem evidence.
- Product & Legal: Approve data residency contracts and communicate constraints for Private deployments.

1) RBAC & Authentication

Overview:
Redwood uses role-based access control (RBAC) layered on platform identity (SSO via Okta) and service principals for automation. Roles are scoped by functional area and least privilege is enforced by default.

Core Roles (examples):
- org_admin: Organization-level administrators (rare; requires two-person approval to grant).
- infra_admin: Cloud and fleet management; can modify IAM roles for compute.
- svc_owner: Service owner with write access to service configs and deployments.
- read_analyst: Read-only access to observability dashboards and logs (redacted PII).
- oncall_incident: Temporary elevated role used during incidents; automatic expiry after 8 hours.

RBAC Implementation Notes:
- All human access is via SSO (Okta) with SCIM provisioning into platform IAM. Service accounts require a short-lived access token minted by the platform's token service.
- Role assignments must reference a documented owner and justification. Changes to role bindings require an approved change ticket and are audited (see Audit Logging).

Minimum Controls and Enforcements:
| Control | Requirement | Enforcement Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| MFA | Enforced for all human SSO accounts | Okta policy (required) |
| Least privilege | Role review every 90 days | Quarterly role certification workflow |
| Temporary elevation | Time-limited elevation for incident responders | Time-bound tokens + audit notification |
| Service account rotation | Keys rotated every 30 days or use short-lived tokens | Deployment pipeline automated rotation |

RBAC Change Process (step-by-step):
1. Request via access-request app with justification and owner.
2. Security reviews for conflicts and SOD (separation of duties).
3. Change is applied via IaC change and automated CI job (pull request).
4. Post-change verification by platform team and recorded evidence in compliance workspace.

2) Audit Logging

Overview:
Comprehensive and tamper-evident audit trails are required for authentication events, RBAC changes, admin API calls, configuration changes, and data-access events that touch customer data. Logs are shipped to the central observability cluster and an immutable archive for compliance evidence.

Log Categories and Retention:
- Auth & Access Logs: 7 years (customer-critical), stored in encrypted archive.
- Platform Control Plane Events (deploys, config changes): 3 years.
- API Access Events (hosted API requests, embeddings): 1 year raw, aggregated metrics retained longer.
- Admin Console Actions: 3 years.

Logging Architecture:
- Agents run on fleet nodes to collect system and application logs (Fluentd -> secure pipeline -> central ELK/Vector).
- All logs are signed at ingestion and a hash chain is stored in the archive to provide tamper evidence.
- Audit logs are indexed with structured fields: timestamp, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource_id, request_id, request_meta.

Alerting and Sampling:
- High-severity auth anomalies (impossible travel, multiple failures) trigger PagerDuty to SecurityOps.
- Sampling kept low for admin actions (no sampling for RBAC changes).

Queries and Evidence Extraction:
- Compliance reviewers have a documented query catalog. Example extraction CMD:

  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVIDENCE_TOKEN' 
    'https://observability.internal/api/v1/audit/search?q=actor:svc_owner+AND+action:grant_role&from=2026-01-01&to=2026-12-31' 

3) Data Residency & Retention

Residency Principles:
- Customer data processed under region-specific agreements is pinned to the chosen region(s) (US, EU, APAC regions supported).
- Control plane metadata may be replicated cross-region unless customer opts out (documented in contract).

Retention Policy (default):
- Customer-generated content (requests/outputs): default 30 days for hosted API; Dedicated and Private deployments default to customer-configurable retention (documented per contract).
- Backups of customer data: encrypted and stored per contract SLA; default 90 days.
- Audit logs: see Audit Logging section.

Enforcement & Verification:
- Data lifecycle is enforced via storage class policies and automated lifecycle jobs (S3 lifecycle transition + delete workflows).
- Regular residency attestation: internal quarterly check that data buckets labeled with 'residency:eu' are not attached to non-EU compute.

Data Deletion and Erasure Requests (30-day SLA):
1. Customer support triages request and assigns to data-ops.
2. Data-ops runs deletion job that removes customer objects, invalidates caches, and records deletion events in audit log.
3. Security verifies deletion and issues an erasure certificate to the customer.

4) Secure SDLC (Software Development Lifecycle)

Requirements for all services shipped by engineering teams:
- Threat modeling at design review for any service exposing external endpoints (must be completed before first external beta).
- Static Application Security Testing (SAST) integrated in CI; critical findings must be resolved before merge.
- Dependency scanning (SCA) with automated policy failures for critical CVEs.
- Secrets scanning on commits and in build artifacts.
- Signed releases: all production images signed with PGP keys stored in HSM/KMS.

Pipeline Controls:
- PRs require two independent reviewers including at least one security reviewer for sensitive services.
- Branch protection: no direct pushes to main; merges via CI that runs unit, integration, and security gates.

Release Checklist (team-run before canary):
1. Unit & integration tests green.
2. SAST and SCA scans pass policy.
3. Load/perf smoke tests for models and runtime.
4. Canary rollout plan with rollback and metrics.
5. Evidence snapshot saved to compliance artifact storage.

5) Incident Response (Security) Procedures

Goals:
- Contain and remediate security incidents with minimal customer impact and clear communications.
- Preserve forensic evidence and produce post-incident compliance artifacts.

Incident Classification:
- Sev1: Data exfiltration, active attacker in production, or production compromise.
- Sev2: Privilege escalation attempt, exposed secret with suspected use.
- Sev3: Minor misconfiguration with low blast radius.

Initial Triage Steps (first 60 minutes):
1. Triage on-call acknowledges and creates a secure incident channel.
2. Capture volatile evidence: snapshot of access logs, process lists, network flows.
3. Apply containment actions (rotate credentials, isolate nodes) and document all actions in the incident log.
4. Notify Security leadership and Legal for Sev1 incidents.

Forensic Evidence Handling:
- All captured evidence must be hashed (SHA-256) and stored in the secure evidence repository. Evidence metadata must include the collector, time, and chain-of-custody owner.

Post-Incident Deliverables:
- Root cause analysis, timeline, remediation plan, and evidence package for compliance reviewers.
- Customer notification template and timeline (Legal approves messaging).

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Quarterly Evidence Runs:
- Security runs a quarterly evidence collection for key controls: RBAC assignments, MFA enforcement, audit logging integrity checks, retention job run logs, SAST/SCA reports for production services.
- Evidence artifacts are stored in the compliance evidence repository (immutable storage with access controls).

Ad-hoc Evidence Requests:
- Requests from auditors or customers are handled by SecurityOps. Requests require an approved NDA and documented scope. Turnaround SLA: 5 business days for standard requests.

Evidence Catalog (examples of artifact IDs):
- RBAC_EXPORT_2027Q1.csv (role assignments as of quarter end).
- LOG_HASH_CHAIN_2027-02-15.bin (log integrity hash chain snapshot).
- SAST_REPORT_service-x_2027-01-10.json (static scan results).

Collectors & Automation:
- Where possible, evidence is generated by automated collectors (IaC drift detector, logging-integrity verifier, build artifact snapshotter). Manual artifacts require an evidence ticket and witness.

7) Risk Exceptions and Approvals

When a team cannot meet a required control due to technical constraints, the team must request a documented risk exception. Exceptions are granted sparingly and for a fixed period with compensating controls.

Risk Exception Process:
1. Submission: Team files an exception request (template) including scope, justification, owner, timeframe, and compensating controls.
2. Security intake review: Security validates technical feasibility and identifies compensating controls.
3. Risk committee review: Quarterly risk committee (Security, Legal, Product) adjudicates and records decision and conditions.
4. Expiry & Re-evaluation: Exceptions automatically expire at end date; teams must re-submit if still required.

Compensating Control Examples:
- Network micro-segmentation and enhanced logging if a service cannot support full encryption in transit due to legacy constraints.
- Additional access reviews and temporary monitoring for services that cannot rotate service account keys on schedule.

Exception Template Fields (required):
- service_name, owner, requested_control_to_waive, justification, compensating_controls, requested_expiry, reviewers_comments.

8) Operational Metrics and SLOs for Controls

Example SLOs:
- RBAC drift detection: 99.9% of unauthorized role bindings detected within 24 hours.
- Audit log delivery: 99.95% of audit events delivered to secure archive within 120 seconds of ingestion.
- Evidence request SLA: 95% of standard auditor evidence delivered within 5 business days.

9) Onboarding and Training

- All new engineers must complete security onboarding: RBAC basics, secrets handling, and incident response primer within their first 14 days.
- Quarterly company-wide tabletop exercises for incident response; teams are scored on containment and evidence preservation.

10) Appendix: Useful Commands and Examples

- Export role bindings (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" 
    https://iam.internal/api/v1/roles/export?format=csv > RBAC_EXPORT_$(date +%F).csv

- Verify log integrity (example):
  sha256sum logs-part-0001.gz > logs-part-0001.gz.sha256
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVIDENCE_TOKEN' -F file=@logs-part-0001.gz.sha256 https://evidence.internal/api/v1/hash-chain/import

- Create incident evidence bundle (example):
  evidence-collector --incident-id INC-2027-0001 --output /secure-evidence/INC-2027-0001.tar.gz --sign-with /keys/forensics-key.pem

Document Maintenance

- Owner: Security team.
- Review cadence: Annual full review or sooner on major control changes or after Sev1 incidents.
- Change log: All changes must reference change ticket and CI artifacts demonstrating implementation.

Questions and Contacts

- Security on-call: security-oncall@redwood.ai (PagerDuty).
- Compliance evidence requests: compliance-evidence@redwood.ai.
- RBAC & IAM questions: iam-owners@redwood.ai.

End of document.
